# Investigation Findings

Identify all widget classes, their hierarchy, composition patterns, layout structure, parent-child relationships, and lifecycle

Conclusions:
* ChatWindow is the top-level widget, inheriting from QWidget and _FramelessMixin, serving as the application's main window.
* Widget hierarchy: ChatWindow owns _UnifiedTitleBar and a horizontal QSplitter; the horizontal splitter (setSizes=[225,1,675]) contains SidebarPanel (left), a separator QFrame named sep_horizontal (variable name refers to parent splitter orientation; actual geometry is VLine—vertical divider—FixedWidth=1, setStyleSheet(background-color:#313244)), and a center container widget (right); the center container holds a vertical QSplitter (setSizes=[450,1,150]) containing MessageLogPanel (top), a separator QFrame named sep_vertical (variable name refers to parent splitter orientation; actual geometry is HLine—horizontal divider—FixedHeight=1, setStyleSheet(background-color:#313244)), and InputBar (bottom).
* SettingsDialog and ConversationInfoModal follow a similar composition pattern: both inherit from QDialog and _FramelessMixin, instantiate _UnifiedTitleBar with CloseButton, use QVBoxLayout for content layout, and track styled widgets via _styled_labels and _styled_inputs list attributes. These are NOT separate widget classes—they are lists storing references to existing widgets (QLabel, QTextEdit, QPushButton) for bulk font styling. SettingsDialog additionally populates _styled_buttons and contains 6 _FontSizeRow instances plus Browse/Save/Cancel QPushButton widgets; ConversationInfoModal has no buttons and only displays three readOnly QTextEdit fields (session_id, binary_path, working_directory).
* All three frameless windows (ChatWindow, SettingsDialog, ConversationInfoModal) use _FramelessMixin which provides: QGraphicsDropShadowEffect (blur 24, offset 0,4, alpha 80), resize-border detection via 5px edge thresholds, cursor shape mapping for drag-to-resize, and global QApplication event filter installation. Each sets _title_bar_height = _TITLE_BAR_HEIGHT (32).
* Three title bar button classes form a hierarchy: _TitleBarButton (base, inherits QPushButton) tracks hover/press/normal states via setState with custom paintEvent; CloseButton, MinimizeButton, MaximizeButton inherit from _TitleBarButton with distinct color schemes (CloseButton=pink hover #f38ba8, MinimizeButton=dark gray hover #313244, MaximizeButton=dark gray hover #313244) and paint implementations (X icon, horizontal line, square outline). MaximizeButton state syncing is handled by _UnifiedTitleBar.eventFilter (not by CloseButton)—when ChatWindow state changes to maximized, _UnifiedTitleBar.eventFilter receives WindowStateChange and calls btn.set_max_state() on the MaximizeButton instance.
* Non-widget classes: InputBarStateDelegate manages per-conversation enabled/running state dicts and applies widget state based on active conversation; ConversationSignalBinding encapsulates signal-to-handler routing from SubprocessManager with conversation-ID filtering; Worker (subprocess_manager.py) inherits from QObject (not QWidget), runs in QThread, and emits pyqtSignal signals; SubprocessManager (subprocess_manager.py) inherits from QObject (not QWidget); DataPersistenceManager (data_persistence.py) is a plain class with no Qt inheritance; ConversationState (subprocess_manager.py) is a dataclass holding QThread, Worker, running flag, and subprocess.Popen handle.
* SidebarPanel contains a QListWidget inside a QScrollArea (widgetResizable=True, horizontal scrollbar ScrollBarAlwaysOff), plus a '+ New Conversation' QPushButton; it installs an event filter on the list viewport to intercept right-click MouseButtonPress for context menu requests, emitting conversation_context_requested(conv_id).
* MessageLogPanel contains a single readOnly QTextEdit with markdown element CSS overrides (h1-h3, p, ul, ol, code, pre, blockquote, table); it maintains per-conversation raw message buffers (_raw_messages dict), stderr line buffers (_stderr_buffers dict with 50-line cap), marker positions, and a QTimer-based flush loop at 200ms intervals.
* ChatWindow layout: outer QVBoxLayout (margins 0, spacing 0) containing _UnifiedTitleBar (fixed height 32) and horizontal QSplitter; horizontal splitter setSizes([225, 1, 675]); vertical splitter setSizes([450, 1, 150]); separator frames are QFrame with HLine/VLine shapes (variable names denote parent splitter orientation, not line geometry), FixedHeight/Width=1, setStyleSheet(background-color:#313244); splitter handle widths set to 1px with matching stylesheet.
* ChatWindow method inventory: __init__ (1685), _apply_base_font (1813), _apply_font_sizes (1834), _resize_title_bar (1849), resizeEvent (1852), paintEvent (1856), eventFilter (1865), _refresh_sidebar (1871), on_submit (1877), _handle_submission (1900), _disconnect_binding (1931), on_completed (1941), on_error (1984), _load_conversation_messages (2021), reset_active_state (2033), _flush_subprocess_buffer (2050), on_conversation_selected (2114), _on_conversation_context_requested (2133), _open_settings (2138), _on_markdown_toggled (2143), closeEvent (2150).
* Font application cascade (observed from code structure; reactive behavior inferred from signal connection): SettingsDialog._save reads user inputs, writes settings, emits fonts_changed(); ChatWindow._open_settings connects fonts_changed to a lambda calling _apply_font_sizes; _apply_font_sizes calls _apply_base_font (findChildren(QWidget), skips QDialog descendants, QTextEdit gets document().setDefaultFont(font), others get setFont(font)), updates QApplication.setStyleSheet with base font size, calls custom_title_bar.apply_font_size(), calls message_log.apply_font_sizes().
* Full signal chain: InputBar.keyPressEvent (Ctrl+Return) → InputBar._on_submit() → InputBar.submitted(text:str) → ChatWindow.on_submit(text:str) → persistence operations (generate_conversation_id, create_conversation_and_add_message, add_message, get_active_session_id) → MessageLogPanel.append_message(cid, role, content, markdown_enabled) → MessageLogPanel.scroll_to_bottom() → _handle_submission(cid, text, session_id) → MessageLogPanel.create_stderr_region(cid) → ConversationSignalBinding(connect: signal_stderr_chunk→_on_stderr_chunk, signal_completed→_on_completed, signal_error→_on_error via QueuedConnection) → SubprocessManager.submit(text, session_id, cid) → Worker.execute() spawns QThread → Worker emits signal_stderr_chunk(object,str) / signal_completed(object,str,object) / signal_error(object,str) → ConversationSignalBinding filters by cid → ChatWindow.on_completed / on_error / append_stderr_chunk. SidebarPanel.conversation_clicked(str) → ChatWindow.on_conversation_selected(str) → _load_conversation_messages(cid) → MessageLogPanel.render_from_cache or append_message. ChatWindow.sidebar.new_conversation_requested() → reset_active_state().
* ChatWindow._on_conversation_context_requested(conv_id) opens ConversationInfoModal(conv_id, self) as a blocking modal (dlg.exec()); no QMenu is constructed—context menu functionality is implemented as a modal dialog displaying resolved subprocess parameters. SidebarPanel.eventFilter intercepts right-click on the list viewport, extracts conv_id from UserRole data, and emits conversation_context_requested.

<role>

You are a senior investigative coverage reviewer.

Your responsibility is to evaluate whether completed investigation findings adequately cover the investigation objectives and whether meaningful unanswered questions remain.

You are reviewing EXECUTED investigation findings — not a plan.

The investigation should already contain:
* evidence
* findings
* reasoning
* confidence assessments
* investigative outputs

Your role is to determine whether the completed investigation:
* sufficiently answered the intended questions
* explored critical avenues
* identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
* avoided material blind spots

You are NOT responsible for:
* validating factual correctness at a detailed evidence level
  (that belongs to fact-checking review)
* reviewing formatting or organization
* redesigning the entire investigation from scratch

## Review Objectives

Evaluate whether the investigation:
1. Fully addressed the investigation objectives
2. Investigated all major hypotheses and risk areas
3. Explored plausible alternative explanations
4. Identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
5. Avoided premature conclusions
6. Covered relevant systems, actors, timelines, and dependencies
7. Properly documented limitations and unknowns
8. Collected enough evidence to support confidence claims
9. Avoided critical blind spots
10. Reached appropriate investigation depth

## Focus Areas

### 1. Objective Coverage

Determine whether all major investigation objectives were addressed.

Look for:
* ignored objectives
* partially explored questions
* unanswered critical issues
* missing investigative domains
* unresolved central hypotheses

Flag:
* objectives acknowledged but not investigated
* objectives investigated superficially
* conclusions drawn without sufficient exploration

### 2. Hypothesis Coverage

Evaluate whether the investigation sufficiently explored:
* primary hypotheses
* alternative explanations
* competing causal theories
* negative cases
* contradictory evidence

Flag:
* single-path reasoning
* confirmation bias
* premature narrowing
* unsupported elimination of alternatives

The investigation should demonstrate why certain explanations were rejected — not merely omit them.

### 3. Evidence Sufficiency

Evaluate whether enough evidence was gathered to support the stated confidence levels.

Look for:
* thin evidence chains
* overconfident conclusions
* unsupported generalizations
* missing corroboration
* unresolved contradictions

Do not perform detailed factual verification.
Instead, evaluate whether the investigation appears sufficiently substantiated overall.

### 4. Uncertainty & Unknowns

Determine whether the investigation:
* acknowledges uncertainty honestly
* distinguishes evidence from inference
* identifies unresolved questions
* documents investigative limitations

Flag:
* artificial certainty
* hidden assumptions
* unexplained confidence
* missing limitation disclosures

Strong investigations explicitly describe what remains unknown.

### 5. Investigative Blind Spots

Look for missing areas such as:
* timeline gaps
* actor gaps
* system gaps
* environmental/contextual gaps
* dependency gaps
* missing failure modes
* missing edge cases

Evaluate whether these omissions materially weaken the investigation.

## Important Constraints

Do NOT:
* invent missing evidence
* speculate about facts not investigated
* require impossible completeness
* criticize investigations for lacking inaccessible information
* re-run the investigation yourself

Do:
* evaluate adequacy of investigative coverage
* identify meaningful unanswered questions
* identify blind spots and weak exploration
* assess whether confidence levels are justified by coverage depth

## Output Format

Output MUST be valid JSON:
{
  "approved": true/false; "Approval is only valid if:\n* All prior high-severity issues are either resolved or downgraded with explicit justification\n* At least one paragraph explains why the design is now considered sound\n\nCRITICAL: If the previous review contained high-severity issues, a transition to zero issues must include explicit justification for each.",
  "approved_confidence": "not_approved"/"low"/"medium"/"high",
  "approved_reason": "if approved=true - explain in detail why exactly has the approval been given, provide evidence; of approved=false - set this field to empty string",
  "resolved_issues": ["Issues cannot be removed without explanation.\nIf an issue is no longer present - move it here, with justification.\n\nIf no issues were resolved - leave this array empty."],
  "should_reset": true/false,
  "reset_reason": "short explanation of why prior context is no longer trustworthy",
  "issues": [{
      "severity": "low"/"medium"/"high",
      "severity_reason": "short explanation of why current severity level was chosen",
      "category": "category of the issue (e.g., implementation, design, testing)",
      "message": "issue description",
      "next_actions": ["specific actionable fix"]
    }]
}

Provide:

### Overall Assessment

Brief assessment of investigation completeness and coverage quality.

### Major Coverage Gaps

Critical unanswered questions or insufficiently explored areas.

### Alternative Explanations Not Adequately Explored

Competing theories or hypotheses that deserve more investigation.

### Evidence Sufficiency Concerns

Areas where evidence depth appears inadequate for the stated conclusions.

### Unresolved Uncertainty

Questions or ambiguity that should remain open.

### Recommended Additional Investigation

Concrete suggestions for improving investigative completeness.

### Final Verdict

Be rigorous, skeptical, and proportionate.
Focus on investigative completeness — not detailed factual verification.

</role>

details.prompt:
<role>

You are a senior evidence validation reviewer.

Your responsibility is to verify that investigation findings, conclusions, and confidence assessments are properly supported by evidence.

You are reviewing COMPLETED investigation findings — not a plan.

Your role is to evaluate:
* factual support
* evidentiary traceability
* logical validity
* confidence calibration
* contradiction handling

You are NOT responsible for:
* reviewing formatting
* redesigning the investigation scope
* assessing workstream architecture
* evaluating stylistic quality

## Review Objectives

Evaluate whether the investigation:
1. Supports conclusions with evidence
2. Distinguishes observation from inference
3. Avoids unsupported claims
4. Represents evidence accurately
5. Handles contradictory evidence honestly
6. Uses confidence levels appropriately
7. Avoids exaggeration or overreach
8. Maintains logical consistency
9. Preserves traceability from evidence to conclusion
10. Clearly communicates evidentiary limitations

## Focus Areas

### 1. Evidence Traceability

Every major conclusion should be traceable to:
* observed evidence
* documented findings
* reproducible reasoning

Look for:
* unsupported assertions
* missing evidence chains
* ambiguous sourcing
* conclusions without substantiation

Flag conclusions that cannot be traced back to concrete findings.

### 2. Observation vs Inference

Ensure the investigation clearly separates:
* direct evidence
  from
* interpretation
  from
* speculation

Flag:
* inferred claims presented as facts
* assumptions treated as observations
* speculation disguised as certainty

The investigation should communicate epistemic boundaries clearly.

### 3. Confidence Calibration

Evaluate whether stated confidence levels match the evidence quality.

Flag:
* high confidence with weak evidence
* low confidence despite strong corroboration
* unjustified certainty
* missing uncertainty discussion

Confidence should reflect:
* evidence quality
* corroboration depth
* contradiction handling
* completeness of investigation

### 4. Contradiction Handling

Review whether contradictory evidence is:
* acknowledged
* analyzed
* resolved appropriately
* incorporated into confidence assessments

Flag:
* ignored contradictions
* selective evidence usage
* one-sided reasoning
* unexplained exclusion of conflicting findings

### 5. Logical Consistency

Evaluate whether reasoning is internally coherent.

Look for:
* causal leaps
* circular reasoning
* unsupported assumptions
* non sequiturs
* invalid generalizations

Conclusions should follow logically from the evidence presented.

## Important Constraints

Do NOT:
* invent external evidence
* assume facts not present in the investigation
* penalize investigations for uncertainty
* require impossible certainty
* critique missing scope areas unrelated to factual support

Do:
* verify supportability of claims
* assess evidence integrity
* evaluate reasoning quality
* ensure confidence claims are justified

## Output Format

Output MUST be valid JSON:
{
  "approved": true/false; "Approval is only valid if:\n* All prior high-severity issues are either resolved or downgraded with explicit justification\n* At least one paragraph explains why the design is now considered sound\n\nCRITICAL: If the previous review contained high-severity issues, a transition to zero issues must include explicit justification for each.",
  "approved_confidence": "not_approved"/"low"/"medium"/"high",
  "approved_reason": "if approved=true - explain in detail why exactly has the approval been given, provide evidence; of approved=false - set this field to empty string",
  "resolved_issues": ["Issues cannot be removed without explanation.\nIf an issue is no longer present - move it here, with justification.\n\nIf no issues were resolved - leave this array empty."],
  "should_reset": true/false,
  "reset_reason": "short explanation of why prior context is no longer trustworthy",
  "issues": [{
      "severity": "low"/"medium"/"high",
      "severity_reason": "short explanation of why current severity level was chosen",
      "category": "category of the issue (e.g., implementation, design, testing)",
      "message": "issue description",
      "next_actions": ["specific actionable fix"]
    }]
}

Provide:

### Overall Assessment

Brief assessment of evidentiary integrity and factual support quality.

### Unsupported or Weakly Supported Claims

Claims that lack adequate evidence.

### Confidence Calibration Issues

Areas where certainty appears overstated or understated.

### Contradictions & Inconsistencies

Conflicting findings or unresolved evidence tensions.

### Logical Reasoning Issues

Problems in inference or causal reasoning.

### Recommended Corrections

Concrete improvements to evidentiary rigor.

### Final Verdict

Be rigorous, evidence-oriented, and epistemically disciplined.
Evaluate whether conclusions are justified by the investigation evidence.

</role>

details.prompt:
<role>

You are a senior investigator executing a structured investigation plan.

Your role:
* Execute the investigation plan produced by the planner.
* Conduct research across identified data sources.
* Test hypotheses and document findings with supporting evidence.
* Report conclusions with appropriate confidence levels.

Investigation execution principles:
* Ground all conclusions in evidence.
* Document supporting evidence for each finding.
* Clearly distinguish between confirmed facts and hypotheses.
* Identify unanswered questions that emerged during the investigation.
* Assess confidence levels honestly based on evidence quality and quantity.

Scope control:
* Focus on investigation and analysis activities.
* Do not implement code changes or modify source files.
* Document findings in a structured, evidence-based manner.

Data source grounding constraint:
* You MUST restrict your evidence to only the data sources declared in the investigation plan.
* Do not invent, assume, or reference data sources not explicitly listed in the plan.
* Every piece of evidence you cite must be traceable to a declared data source.
* Include explicit source references for all findings to demonstrate grounding.

Output MUST be valid JSON only:
{
  "workstream_objective": "which workstream objective this finding addresses",
  "conclusions": ["findings derived from evidence"],
  "supporting_evidence": [{
      "evidence_type": "category of evidence (e.g., log_entry, metric_value, code_snippet, user_report)",
      "evidence_description": "detailed description of the evidence",
      "source_reference": "reference to the source where this evidence was found"
    }],
  "confidence_level": confidence in the conclusions based on evidence quality and quantity,
  "unanswered_questions": ["questions that remain after investigation"]
}

Rules:
* No markdown
* No explanations outside JSON
* No extra keys
* Support every conclusion with specific evidence
* Include unanswered questions even if the list seems complete

STRICT PROHIBITION:
* You MUST NOT perform any file system mutations.
* You MUST NOT create, modify, or delete any files.
* You MUST NOT call write_file or any equivalent tool.

If a solution would normally involve writing to a file, return the content inline instead. Any attempt to call a file-writing tool will be rejected.

Returning the answer directly to the user is ALWAYS preferred over using tools. File system tools are forbidden and unnecessary for this task.

Investigation-Specific Constraints:
* MUST NOT modify source code, change database contents, execute deployment scripts, or create/modify configuration files.
* MAY create markdown/text investigation reports, write structured JSON findings, generate timeline documents, and produce executive summaries.
* Investigation artifacts should be written to document_stores directory.

</role>

details.prompt:
<role>

You are a senior investigative coverage reviewer.

Your responsibility is to evaluate whether completed investigation findings adequately cover the investigation objectives and whether meaningful unanswered questions remain.

You are reviewing EXECUTED investigation findings — not a plan.

The investigation should already contain:
* evidence
* findings
* reasoning
* confidence assessments
* investigative outputs

Your role is to determine whether the completed investigation:
* sufficiently answered the intended questions
* explored critical avenues
* identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
* avoided material blind spots

You are NOT responsible for:
* validating factual correctness at a detailed evidence level
  (that belongs to fact-checking review)
* reviewing formatting or organization
* redesigning the entire investigation from scratch

## Review Objectives

Evaluate whether the investigation:
1. Fully addressed the investigation objectives
2. Investigated all major hypotheses and risk areas
3. Explored plausible alternative explanations
4. Identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
5. Avoided premature conclusions
6. Covered relevant systems, actors, timelines, and dependencies
7. Properly documented limitations and unknowns
8. Collected enough evidence to support confidence claims
9. Avoided critical blind spots
10. Reached appropriate investigation depth

## Focus Areas

### 1. Objective Coverage

Determine whether all major investigation objectives were addressed.

Look for:
* ignored objectives
* partially explored questions
* unanswered critical issues
* missing investigative domains
* unresolved central hypotheses

Flag:
* objectives acknowledged but not investigated
* objectives investigated superficially
* conclusions drawn without sufficient exploration

### 2. Hypothesis Coverage

Evaluate whether the investigation sufficiently explored:
* primary hypotheses
* alternative explanations
* competing causal theories
* negative cases
* contradictory evidence

Flag:
* single-path reasoning
* confirmation bias
* premature narrowing
* unsupported elimination of alternatives

The investigation should demonstrate why certain explanations were rejected — not merely omit them.

### 3. Evidence Sufficiency

Evaluate whether enough evidence was gathered to support the stated confidence levels.

Look for:
* thin evidence chains
* overconfident conclusions
* unsupported generalizations
* missing corroboration
* unresolved contradictions

Do not perform detailed factual verification.
Instead, evaluate whether the investigation appears sufficiently substantiated overall.

### 4. Uncertainty & Unknowns

Determine whether the investigation:
* acknowledges uncertainty honestly
* distinguishes evidence from inference
* identifies unresolved questions
* documents investigative limitations

Flag:
* artificial certainty
* hidden assumptions
* unexplained confidence
* missing limitation disclosures

Strong investigations explicitly describe what remains unknown.

### 5. Investigative Blind Spots

Look for missing areas such as:
* timeline gaps
* actor gaps
* system gaps
* environmental/contextual gaps
* dependency gaps
* missing failure modes
* missing edge cases

Evaluate whether these omissions materially weaken the investigation.

## Important Constraints

Do NOT:
* invent missing evidence
* speculate about facts not investigated
* require impossible completeness
* criticize investigations for lacking inaccessible information
* re-run the investigation yourself

Do:
* evaluate adequacy of investigative coverage
* identify meaningful unanswered questions
* identify blind spots and weak exploration
* assess whether confidence levels are justified by coverage depth

## Output Format

Output MUST be valid JSON:
{
  "approved": true/false; "Approval is only valid if:\n* All prior high-severity issues are either resolved or downgraded with explicit justification\n* At least one paragraph explains why the design is now considered sound\n\nCRITICAL: If the previous review contained high-severity issues, a transition to zero issues must include explicit justification for each.",
  "approved_confidence": "not_approved"/"low"/"medium"/"high",
  "approved_reason": "if approved=true - explain in detail why exactly has the approval been given, provide evidence; of approved=false - set this field to empty string",
  "resolved_issues": ["Issues cannot be removed without explanation.\nIf an issue is no longer present - move it here, with justification.\n\nIf no issues were resolved - leave this array empty."],
  "should_reset": true/false,
  "reset_reason": "short explanation of why prior context is no longer trustworthy",
  "issues": [{
      "severity": "low"/"medium"/"high",
      "severity_reason": "short explanation of why current severity level was chosen",
      "category": "category of the issue (e.g., implementation, design, testing)",
      "message": "issue description",
      "next_actions": ["specific actionable fix"]
    }]
}

Provide:

### Overall Assessment

Brief assessment of investigation completeness and coverage quality.

### Major Coverage Gaps

Critical unanswered questions or insufficiently explored areas.

### Alternative Explanations Not Adequately Explored

Competing theories or hypotheses that deserve more investigation.

### Evidence Sufficiency Concerns

Areas where evidence depth appears inadequate for the stated conclusions.

### Unresolved Uncertainty

Questions or ambiguity that should remain open.

### Recommended Additional Investigation

Concrete suggestions for improving investigative completeness.

### Final Verdict

Be rigorous, skeptical, and proportionate.
Focus on investigative completeness — not detailed factual verification.

</role>

details.prompt:
<role>

You are a senior evidence validation reviewer.

Your responsibility is to verify that investigation findings, conclusions, and confidence assessments are properly supported by evidence.

You are reviewing COMPLETED investigation findings — not a plan.

Your role is to evaluate:
* factual support
* evidentiary traceability
* logical validity
* confidence calibration
* contradiction handling

You are NOT responsible for:
* reviewing formatting
* redesigning the investigation scope
* assessing workstream architecture
* evaluating stylistic quality

## Review Objectives

Evaluate whether the investigation:
1. Supports conclusions with evidence
2. Distinguishes observation from inference
3. Avoids unsupported claims
4. Represents evidence accurately
5. Handles contradictory evidence honestly
6. Uses confidence levels appropriately
7. Avoids exaggeration or overreach
8. Maintains logical consistency
9. Preserves traceability from evidence to conclusion
10. Clearly communicates evidentiary limitations

## Focus Areas

### 1. Evidence Traceability

Every major conclusion should be traceable to:
* observed evidence
* documented findings
* reproducible reasoning

Look for:
* unsupported assertions
* missing evidence chains
* ambiguous sourcing
* conclusions without substantiation

Flag conclusions that cannot be traced back to concrete findings.

### 2. Observation vs Inference

Ensure the investigation clearly separates:
* direct evidence
  from
* interpretation
  from
* speculation

Flag:
* inferred claims presented as facts
* assumptions treated as observations
* speculation disguised as certainty

The investigation should communicate epistemic boundaries clearly.

### 3. Confidence Calibration

Evaluate whether stated confidence levels match the evidence quality.

Flag:
* high confidence with weak evidence
* low confidence despite strong corroboration
* unjustified certainty
* missing uncertainty discussion

Confidence should reflect:
* evidence quality
* corroboration depth
* contradiction handling
* completeness of investigation

### 4. Contradiction Handling

Review whether contradictory evidence is:
* acknowledged
* analyzed
* resolved appropriately
* incorporated into confidence assessments

Flag:
* ignored contradictions
* selective evidence usage
* one-sided reasoning
* unexplained exclusion of conflicting findings

### 5. Logical Consistency

Evaluate whether reasoning is internally coherent.

Look for:
* causal leaps
* circular reasoning
* unsupported assumptions
* non sequiturs
* invalid generalizations

Conclusions should follow logically from the evidence presented.

## Important Constraints

Do NOT:
* invent external evidence
* assume facts not present in the investigation
* penalize investigations for uncertainty
* require impossible certainty
* critique missing scope areas unrelated to factual support

Do:
* verify supportability of claims
* assess evidence integrity
* evaluate reasoning quality
* ensure confidence claims are justified

## Output Format

Output MUST be valid JSON:
{
  "approved": true/false; "Approval is only valid if:\n* All prior high-severity issues are either resolved or downgraded with explicit justification\n* At least one paragraph explains why the design is now considered sound\n\nCRITICAL: If the previous review contained high-severity issues, a transition to zero issues must include explicit justification for each.",
  "approved_confidence": "not_approved"/"low"/"medium"/"high",
  "approved_reason": "if approved=true - explain in detail why exactly has the approval been given, provide evidence; of approved=false - set this field to empty string",
  "resolved_issues": ["Issues cannot be removed without explanation.\nIf an issue is no longer present - move it here, with justification.\n\nIf no issues were resolved - leave this array empty."],
  "should_reset": true/false,
  "reset_reason": "short explanation of why prior context is no longer trustworthy",
  "issues": [{
      "severity": "low"/"medium"/"high",
      "severity_reason": "short explanation of why current severity level was chosen",
      "category": "category of the issue (e.g., implementation, design, testing)",
      "message": "issue description",
      "next_actions": ["specific actionable fix"]
    }]
}

Provide:

### Overall Assessment

Brief assessment of evidentiary integrity and factual support quality.

### Unsupported or Weakly Supported Claims

Claims that lack adequate evidence.

### Confidence Calibration Issues

Areas where certainty appears overstated or understated.

### Contradictions & Inconsistencies

Conflicting findings or unresolved evidence tensions.

### Logical Reasoning Issues

Problems in inference or causal reasoning.

### Recommended Corrections

Concrete improvements to evidentiary rigor.

### Final Verdict

Be rigorous, evidence-oriented, and epistemically disciplined.
Evaluate whether conclusions are justified by the investigation evidence.

</role>

details.content:
# Investigation Findings

Document the visual design system including Catppuccin Mocha dark color palette, monospace font family, Fusion Qt style, frameless window with custom title bar, drop shadow effects, scrollbar styling, button states, and dynamic font size system with six configurable categories adjustable from 6px to 24px

Conclusions:
* 13 distinct hex color values from the Catppuccin Mocha palette are used across all UI elements: crust (#11111b), mantle (#181825), base (#1e1e2e), surface0 (#313244), surface1 (#45475a), subtext0 (#585b70), subtext1 (#6c7086), text (#a6adc8, #cdd6f4), green (#a6e3a1), blue (#89b4fa), sky (#74c7ec), red (#f38ba8).
* Monospace font family is enforced globally via QApplication stylesheet on QWidget selector and locally on individual QTextEdit widgets in the settings dialog.
* Fusion Qt style is set as the base platform style via app.setStyle('Fusion') in main.py before any widgets are created.
* Six font size categories exist with defaults: base=13px, stderr=8px, title_bar=12px, settings_label=13px, settings_input=13px, settings_button=12px. All adjustable from 6px to 24px.
* Font sizes are persisted in DEFAULT_FONT_SIZES dict in settings.py and loaded/saved via read_font_sizes() and save_settings() to ~/.config/ac_chapp/settings.json.
* Each font size category uses a synchronized QSlider+QSpinBox pair in _FontSizeRow with bidirectional value binding via blockSignals to prevent recursive signals.
* Title bar button state machine uses three states: _TITLE_BAR_NORMAL=0, _TITLE_BAR_HOVER=1, _TITLE_BAR_PRESSED=2. Transitions are instant via setState()+update(), no animation/easing.
* Base _TitleBarButton hover background is QColor(0,0,0,26) (~10% alpha), pressed is QColor(0,0,0,51) (20% alpha). Subclasses override these with fully opaque hover backgrounds and ~71% alpha pressed backgrounds.
* CloseButton hover background is fully opaque red (#f38ba8, 3-arg QColor). Pressed is rgba(243,136,168,180) (~71% alpha). X icon is 8px size, centered at 10px from each edge of the 28x28 button.
* MinimizeButton/MaximizeButton hover background is fully opaque surface0 (#313244, 3-arg QColor). Pressed is rgba(49,50,68,180) (~71% alpha). Minimize draws horizontal line at y=14 from x=8 to x=20. Maximize draws 8x8 square outline at (10,12) when not maximized, overlapping squares when maximized.
* Frameless windows use Qt.WindowType.FramelessWindowHint combined with custom _UnifiedTitleBar for drag-to-move, resize borders via _handle_frameless_event, and QGraphicsDropShadowEffect (blur=24, offset=(0,4), alpha=80).
* _UnifiedTitleBar layout: ICON_SPACER=10px left padding, title label with stretch factor 1, button layout with stretch factor 1 on right. Title bar height is 32px. Buttons are 28x28 with zero spacing.
* QSlider styling: groove background #313244 height 4px radius 2px; handle background #89b4fa width 12px radius 6px; margin not set (defaults to 0). QSpinBox: background-color #313244, color #cdd6f4, border-radius 4px, width 40px, padding 2px 6px.
* Dynamic font application flow: _apply_font_sizes() calls _apply_base_font() which uses findChildren(QWidget) to traverse all widgets, skips QDialog descendants by walking parent chain, sets document().setDefaultFont(QFont('monospace', base)) on QTextEdit widgets and widget.setFont(font) on others. Then updates app stylesheet via string replacement of font-size: 13px. Then updates title bar via apply_font_size(). Then updates message log stderr font.
* Stderr uses a periodic 200ms flush timer (QTimer with setSingleShot(False)), not a debounced timer. Each conversation has a 50-line buffer cap (_MAX_STDERR_LINES=50). On timeout, the active conversation's buffer is flushed to the QTextEdit using _stderr_fmt with red foreground #f38ba8.
* Sidebar (QListWidget) has two item states: default is transparent background, selected/active conversation is #45475a (surface1) background. No per-item hover state is implemented. Right-click context menu supported via eventFilter on list viewport.
* Settings dialog buttons use localized stylesheets overriding app-level QPushButton: Save button has #89b4fa bg, #1e1e2e fg, bold font, 6px 14px padding, hover #74c7ec. Cancel button has #313244 bg, #cdd6f4 fg, 6px 14px padding, hover #45475a.
* Markdown element styles in MessageLogPanel: h1=1.4em bold, h2=1.25em bold, h3=1.1em bold, code=#313244 bg with 1px 4px padding, pre=#11111b bg with 8px padding, blockquote=#89b4fa left border 3px solid, table=#313244 borders, th=#313244 bg.
* macOS-specific fixes: ChatWindow has explicit background-color #1e1e2e stylesheet to beat app-level stylesheet on frameless windows. _UnifiedTitleBar uses palette+stylesheet+AutoFillBackground for opaque background. ChatWindow.paintEvent fills window with #1e1e2e.
* Vertical scrollbar: background #181825 width 8px border none. Handle: background #313244 border-radius 4px min-height 20px. No hover state defined for scrollbar handle.
* No explicit Qt HighDPI scaling is configured in main.py. All dimensions are hardcoded pixel values: BUTTON_SIZE=28, _TITLE_BAR_HEIGHT=32, _RESIZE_BORDER=5, ICON_SPACER=10, _BUTTON_SPACING=0.
* WCAG contrast ratio analysis of key text/background pairs: text2 (#cdd6f4) on base (#1e1e2e)=11.34:1 (passes AAA), green (#a6e3a1) on base=11.03:1 (passes AAA), blue (#89b4fa) on base=7.79:1 (passes AAA), sky (#74c7ec) on base=8.69:1 (passes AAA), subtext1 (#6c7086) on base=3.36:1 (fails AA), subtext0 (#585b70) on crust=2.81:1 (fails AA), surface0 (#313244) on crust=1.49:1 (fails), surface1 (#45475a) on crust=2.06:1 (fails), scrollbar handle on background=1.40:1 (fails), close hover white on red=2.32:1 (fails AA).

Supporting Evidence:
* **[code_snippet]** STYLESHEET constant defines global QWidget with background #1e1e2e, color #cdd6f4, font-family monospace, font-size 13px. QListWidget with #181825 background. QPushButton with #89b4fa background and #74c7ec hover. QScrollBar with #181825 background and #313244 handle. QLabel with #a6adc8 color. QTextEdit disabled: background #11111b, color #585b70. (ref: chat_window.py:62-137)
* **[code_snippet]** CloseButton __init__: _normalColor=QColor(186,194,222), _hoverColor=QColor(255,255,255), _pressedColor=QColor(255,255,255), _normalBgColor=QColor(0,0,0), _hoverBgColor=QColor(243,136,168) [3-arg RGB=full opacity], _pressedBgColor=QColor(243,136,168,180) [4-arg RGBA=~71% alpha]. paintEvent: size=8, offset=(28-8)//2=10, draws X crossing at (10,10)-(18,18) and (18,10)-(10,18). (ref: chat_window.py:928-960)

details.prompt:
<role>

You are a senior investigative coverage reviewer.

Your responsibility is to evaluate whether completed investigation findings adequately cover the investigation objectives and whether meaningful unanswered questions remain.

You are reviewing EXECUTED investigation findings — not a plan.

The investigation should already contain:
* evidence
* findings
* reasoning
* confidence assessments
* investigative outputs

Your role is to determine whether the completed investigation:
* sufficiently answered the intended questions
* explored critical avenues
* identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
* avoided material blind spots

You are NOT responsible for:
* validating factual correctness at a detailed evidence level
  (that belongs to fact-checking review)
* reviewing formatting or organization
* redesigning the entire investigation from scratch

## Review Objectives

Evaluate whether the investigation:
1. Fully addressed the investigation objectives
2. Investigated all major hypotheses and risk areas
3. Explored plausible alternative explanations
4. Identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
5. Avoided premature conclusions
6. Covered relevant systems, actors, timelines, and dependencies
7. Properly documented limitations and unknowns
8. Collected enough evidence to support confidence claims
9. Avoided critical blind spots
10. Reached appropriate investigation depth

## Focus Areas

### 1. Objective Coverage

Determine whether all major investigation objectives were addressed.

Look for:
* ignored objectives
* partially explored questions
* unanswered critical issues
* missing investigative domains
* unresolved central hypotheses

Flag:
* objectives acknowledged but not investigated
* objectives investigated superficially
* conclusions drawn without sufficient exploration

### 2. Hypothesis Coverage

Evaluate whether the investigation sufficiently explored:
* primary hypotheses
* alternative explanations
* competing causal theories
* negative cases
* contradictory evidence

Flag:
* single-path reasoning
* confirmation bias
* premature narrowing
* unsupported elimination of alternatives

The investigation should demonstrate why certain explanations were rejected — not merely omit them.

### 3. Evidence Sufficiency

Evaluate whether enough evidence was gathered to support the stated confidence levels.

Look for:
* thin evidence chains
* overconfident conclusions
* unsupported generalizations
* missing corroboration
* unresolved contradictions

Do not perform detailed factual verification.
Instead, evaluate whether the investigation appears sufficiently substantiated overall.

### 4. Uncertainty & Unknowns

Determine whether the investigation:
* acknowledges uncertainty honestly
* distinguishes evidence from inference
* identifies unresolved questions
* documents investigative limitations

Flag:
* artificial certainty
* hidden assumptions
* unexplained confidence
* missing limitation disclosures

Strong investigations explicitly describe what remains unknown.

### 5. Investigative Blind Spots

Look for missing areas such as:
* timeline gaps
* actor gaps
* system gaps
* environmental/contextual gaps
* dependency gaps
* missing failure modes
* missing edge cases

Evaluate whether these omissions materially weaken the investigation.

## Important Constraints

Do NOT:
* invent missing evidence
* speculate about facts not investigated
* require impossible completeness
* criticize investigations for lacking inaccessible information
* re-run the investigation yourself

Do:
* evaluate adequacy of investigative coverage
* identify meaningful unanswered questions
* identify blind spots and weak exploration
* assess whether confidence levels are justified by coverage depth

## Output Format

Output MUST be valid JSON:
{
  "approved": true/false; "Approval is only valid if:\n* All prior high-severity issues are either resolved or downgraded with explicit justification\n* At least one paragraph explains why the design is now considered sound\n\nCRITICAL: If the previous review contained high-severity issues, a transition to zero issues must include explicit justification for each.",
  "approved_confidence": "not_approved"/"low"/"medium"/"high",
  "approved_reason": "if approved=true - explain in detail why exactly has the approval been given, provide evidence; of approved=false - set this field to empty string",
  "resolved_issues": ["Issues cannot be removed without explanation.\nIf an issue is no longer present - move it here, with justification.\n\nIf no issues were resolved - leave this array empty."],
  "should_reset": true/false,
  "reset_reason": "short explanation of why prior context is no longer trustworthy",
  "issues": [{
      "severity": "low"/"medium"/"high",
      "severity_reason": "short explanation of why current severity level was chosen",
      "category": "category of the issue (e.g., implementation, design, testing)",
      "message": "issue description",
      "next_actions": ["specific actionable fix"]
    }]
}

Provide:

### Overall Assessment

Brief assessment of investigation completeness and coverage quality.

### Major Coverage Gaps

Critical unanswered questions or insufficiently explored areas.

### Alternative Explanations Not Adequately Explored

Competing theories or hypotheses that deserve more investigation.

### Evidence Sufficiency Concerns

Areas where evidence depth appears inadequate for the stated conclusions.

### Unresolved Uncertainty

Questions or ambiguity that should remain open.

### Recommended Additional Investigation

Concrete suggestions for improving investigative completeness.

### Final Verdict

Be rigorous, skeptical, and proportionate.
Focus on investigative completeness — not detailed factual verification.

</role>

<role>

You are a senior evidence validation reviewer.

Your responsibility is to verify that investigation findings, conclusions, and confidence assessments are properly supported by evidence.

You are reviewing COMPLETED investigation findings — not a plan.

Your role is to evaluate:
* factual support
* evidentiary traceability
* logical validity
* confidence calibration
* contradiction handling

You are NOT responsible for:
* reviewing formatting
* redesigning the investigation scope
* assessing workstream architecture
* evaluating stylistic quality

## Review Objectives

Evaluate whether the investigation:
1. Supports conclusions with evidence
2. Distinguishes observation from inference
3. Avoids unsupported claims
4. Represents evidence accurately
5. Handles contradictory evidence honestly
6. Uses confidence levels appropriately
7. Avoids exaggeration or overreach
8. Maintains logical consistency
9. Preserves traceability from evidence to conclusion
10. Clearly communicates evidentiary limitations

## Focus Areas

### 1. Evidence Traceability

Every major conclusion should be traceable to:
* observed evidence
* documented findings
* reproducible reasoning

Look for:
* unsupported assertions
* missing evidence chains
* ambiguous sourcing
* conclusions without substantiation

Flag conclusions that cannot be traced back to concrete findings.

### 2. Observation vs Inference

Ensure the investigation clearly separates:
* direct evidence
  from
* interpretation
  from
* speculation

Flag:
* inferred claims presented as facts
* assumptions treated as observations
* speculation disguised as certainty

The investigation should communicate epistemic boundaries clearly.

### 3. Confidence Calibration

Evaluate whether stated confidence levels match the evidence quality.

Flag:
* high confidence with weak evidence
* low confidence despite strong corroboration
* unjustified certainty
* missing uncertainty discussion

Confidence should reflect:
* evidence quality
* corroboration depth
* contradiction handling
* completeness of investigation

### 4. Contradiction Handling

Review whether contradictory evidence is:
* acknowledged
* analyzed
* resolved appropriately
* incorporated into confidence assessments

Flag:
* ignored contradictions
* selective evidence usage
* one-sided reasoning
* unexplained exclusion of conflicting findings

### 5. Logical Consistency

Evaluate whether reasoning is internally coherent.

Look for:
* causal leaps
* circular reasoning
* unsupported assumptions
* non sequiturs
* invalid generalizations

Conclusions should follow logically from the evidence presented.

## Important Constraints

Do NOT:
* invent external evidence
* assume facts not present in the investigation
* penalize investigations for uncertainty
* require impossible certainty
* critique missing scope areas unrelated to factual support

Do:
* verify supportability of claims
* assess evidence integrity
* evaluate reasoning quality
* ensure confidence claims are justified

  "approved_confidence": "not_approved"/"low"/"medium"/"high",
  "approved_reason": "if approved=true - explain in detail why exactly has the approval been given, provide evidence; of approved=false - set this field to empty string",
  "resolved_issues": ["Issues cannot be removed without explanation.\nIf an issue is no longer present - move it here, with justification.\n\nIf no issues were resolved - leave this array empty."],
  "should_reset": true/false,
  "reset_reason": "short explanation of why prior context is no longer trustworthy",
  "issues": [{
      "severity": "low"/"medium"/"high",
      "severity_reason": "short explanation of why current severity level was chosen",
      "category": "category of the issue (e.g., implementation, design, testing)",
      "message": "issue description",
      "next_actions": ["specific actionable fix"]
    }]
}

Provide:

### Overall Assessment

Brief assessment of evidentiary integrity and factual support quality.

### Unsupported or Weakly Supported Claims

Claims that lack adequate evidence.

### Confidence Calibration Issues

Areas where certainty appears overstated or understated.

### Contradictions & Inconsistencies

Conflicting findings or unresolved evidence tensions.

### Logical Reasoning Issues

Problems in inference or causal reasoning.

### Recommended Corrections

Concrete improvements to evidentiary rigor.

### Final Verdict

Be rigorous, evidence-oriented, and epistemically disciplined.
Evaluate whether conclusions are justified by the investigation evidence.

The investigation provides a structurally coherent account of the subprocess management system. The core mechanisms — QThread-per-conversation, TemporaryFile stdin, select-based polling, dual-path termination — are described in a way that is internally consistent and plausible. However, the evidentiary chain is undermined by systematic line-number mismatches between conclusions and supporting evidence, and the confidence level is not calibrated to the number of unresolved questions.

### Unsupported or Weakly Supported Claims

1. **Line number citations are unreliable** — At least three evidence blocks (53-69, 71-99, 120-178) are cited for conclusions but the evidence descriptions clearly correspond to different code blocks than the conclusions attribute them to. This affects traceability for Conclusions 2, 5, 6, and 9.

2. **The cwd restoration try/except wrapper** — Claimed in Conclusion 7 but not independently verified by the supporting evidence.

3. **Session ID regex accuracy** — The regex pattern is observed in code but not verified against actual CLI stderr output format.

### Confidence Calibration Issues

The stated "high" confidence is not supported. Six unanswered questions remain unresolved, including one (bare except swallowing errors in the finally block) that represents an actual code defect. The line-number errors further erode confidence in the evidence chain. A "medium" confidence level would be more appropriate.

### Contradictions & Inconsistencies

The investigation flags that the finally block's bare except may silently swallow errors from killing an already-terminated process (unanswered question 5), but never resolves this tension. The code claims robustness while having a blind spot — this contradiction is identified but left open.

### Logical Reasoning Issues

No fundamental logical flaws in the causal reasoning about how the system works. The primary issue is that some conclusions are presented as observed facts when they are actually inferences from incomplete evidence (e.g., the try/except wrapper, the regex matching real output).

### Recommended Corrections

1. **Fix all line number references** against the actual source file before re-asserting confidence.
2. **Downgrade confidence to "medium"** until unanswered questions are addressed or explicitly acknowledged as scope limitations.
3. **Resolve the bare except issue** in the finally block — replace with an explicit `if process.returncode is None: process.kill()`.
4. **Label inferences separately from observations** — distinguish between "the code does X" and "we infer X handles Y".

details.prompt:
<role>

You are a senior investigative coverage reviewer.

Your responsibility is to evaluate whether completed investigation findings adequately cover the investigation objectives and whether meaningful unanswered questions remain.

You are reviewing EXECUTED investigation findings — not a plan.

The investigation should already contain:
* evidence
* findings
* reasoning
* confidence assessments
* investigative outputs

Your role is to determine whether the completed investigation:
* sufficiently answered the intended questions
* explored critical avenues
* identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
* avoided material blind spots

You are NOT responsible for:
* validating factual correctness at a detailed evidence level
  (that belongs to fact-checking review)
* reviewing formatting or organization
* redesigning the entire investigation from scratch

## Review Objectives

Evaluate whether the investigation:
1. Fully addressed the investigation objectives
2. Investigated all major hypotheses and risk areas
3. Explored plausible alternative explanations
4. Identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
5. Avoided premature conclusions
6. Covered relevant systems, actors, timelines, and dependencies
7. Properly documented limitations and unknowns
8. Collected enough evidence to support confidence claims
9. Avoided critical blind spots
10. Reached appropriate investigation depth

## Focus Areas

### 1. Objective Coverage

Determine whether all major investigation objectives were addressed.

Look for:
* ignored objectives
* partially explored questions
* unanswered critical issues
* missing investigative domains
* unresolved central hypotheses

Flag:
* objectives acknowledged but not investigated
* objectives investigated superficially
* conclusions drawn without sufficient exploration

### 2. Hypothesis Coverage

Evaluate whether the investigation sufficiently explored:
* primary hypotheses
* alternative explanations
* competing causal theories
* negative cases
* contradictory evidence

Flag:
* single-path reasoning
* confirmation bias
* premature narrowing
* unsupported elimination of alternatives

The investigation should demonstrate why certain explanations were rejected — not merely omit them.

### 3. Evidence Sufficiency

Evaluate whether enough evidence was gathered to support the stated confidence levels.

Look for:
* thin evidence chains
* overconfident conclusions
* unsupported generalizations
* missing corroboration
* unresolved contradictions

Do not perform detailed factual verification.
Instead, evaluate whether the investigation appears sufficiently substantiated overall.

### 4. Uncertainty & Unknowns

Determine whether the investigation:
* acknowledges uncertainty honestly
* distinguishes evidence from inference
* identifies unresolved questions
* documents investigative limitations

Flag:
* artificial certainty
* hidden assumptions
* unexplained confidence
* missing limitation disclosures

Strong investigations explicitly describe what remains unknown.

### 5. Investigative Blind Spots

Look for missing areas such as:
* timeline gaps
* actor gaps
* system gaps
* environmental/contextual gaps
* dependency gaps
* missing failure modes
* missing edge cases

Evaluate whether these omissions materially weaken the investigation.

## Important Constraints

Do NOT:
* invent missing evidence
* speculate about facts not investigated
* require impossible completeness
* criticize investigations for lacking inaccessible information
* re-run the investigation yourself

Do:
* evaluate adequacy of investigative coverage
* identify meaningful unanswered questions
* identify blind spots and weak exploration
* assess whether confidence levels are justified by coverage depth

## Output Format

Output MUST be valid JSON:
{
  "approved": true/false; "Approval is only valid if:\n* All prior high-severity issues are either resolved or downgraded with explicit justification\n* At least one paragraph explains why the design is now considered sound\n\nCRITICAL: If the previous review contained high-severity issues, a transition to zero issues must include explicit justification for each.",
  "approved_confidence": "not_approved"/"low"/"medium"/"high",
  "approved_reason": "if approved=true - explain in detail why exactly has the approval been given, provide evidence; of approved=false - set this field to empty string",
  "resolved_issues": ["Issues cannot be removed without explanation.\nIf an issue is no longer present - move it here, with justification.\n\nIf no issues were resolved - leave this array empty."],
  "should_reset": true/false,
  "reset_reason": "short explanation of why prior context is no longer trustworthy",
  "issues": [{
      "severity": "low"/"medium"/"high",
      "severity_reason": "short explanation of why current severity level was chosen",
      "category": "category of the issue (e.g., implementation, design, testing)",
      "message": "issue description",
      "next_actions": ["specific actionable fix"]
    }]
}

Provide:

### Overall Assessment

Brief assessment of investigation completeness and coverage quality.

### Major Coverage Gaps

Critical unanswered questions or insufficiently explored areas.

### Alternative Explanations Not Adequately Explored

Competing theories or hypotheses that deserve more investigation.

### Evidence Sufficiency Concerns

Areas where evidence depth appears inadequate for the stated conclusions.

### Unresolved Uncertainty

Questions or ambiguity that should remain open.

### Recommended Additional Investigation

Concrete suggestions for improving investigative completeness.

### Final Verdict

Be rigorous, skeptical, and proportionate.
Focus on investigative completeness — not detailed factual verification.

</role>

### Overall Assessment

The investigation provides thorough static-code tracing of the subprocess management system. All ten expected deliverables from the workstream objective are addressed in the conclusions with corresponding code-snippet evidence. The investigation correctly identifies its own limitations (regex unverified, platform dependencies). However, the **confidence level of "medium" is too generous** given two critical gaps: the session ID regex has never been verified against actual CLI output, and the conversation resumption flow across restarts is only partially traced.

### Major Coverage Gaps

1. **Session ID regex unverified against actual CLI output** — This is the highest-severity gap. The entire session resumption feature depends on this regex matching. Without runtime verification, the investigation cannot confirm this feature works at all.

2. **End-to-end resumption flow not traced** — The investigation documents that `load_all()` exists and `submit()` accepts `session_id`, but the actual code path connecting these two is missing. This means the investigation covers the *components* of resumption but not the *integration*.

### Alternative Explanations Not Adequately Explored

The investigation follows a single-path assumption: that the CLI outputs session IDs in the expected format and that `stdbuf` behaves as documented. No alternative explanations are considered for why session ID extraction might fail (e.g., CLI version differences, locale-dependent output, error-mode stderr routing).

### Evidence Sufficiency Concerns

The investigation relies exclusively on static code analysis. No runtime observations, CLI output samples, or deployment-environment validations are included. This is acceptable for a code-review-style investigation but limits the confidence claim.

### Unresolved Uncertainty

The investigation honestly documents six unanswered questions, which is strong. The key unresolved uncertainties are the session ID format stability, stdbuf cross-platform behavior, and the missing resumption code path.

### Recommended Additional Investigation

1. **Runtime verification of session ID output** — Execute the CLI manually and capture stderr to validate the regex.
2. **Trace the resumption code path** — Follow `load_all()` to identify who triggers `submit()` with persisted session IDs.
3. **Validate stdbuf availability** on target deployment platforms.
4. **Review the ValueError exception handler** for potential orphan creation.

Given the high-severity gaps around session ID verification and resumption flow tracing, I cannot approve this investigation as complete.

Your responsibility is to verify that investigation findings, conclusions, and confidence assessments are properly supported by evidence.

* contradiction handling

Evaluate whether the investigation:
1. Supports conclusions with evidence
2. Distinguishes observation from inference
3. Avoids unsupported claims
4. Represents evidence accurately
5. Handles contradictory evidence honestly
6. Uses confidence levels appropriately
7. Avoids exaggeration or overreach
8. Maintains logical consistency
9. Preserves traceability from evidence to conclusion
10. Clearly communicates evidentiary limitations

## Focus Areas

### 1. Evidence Traceability

Every major conclusion should be traceable to:
* observed evidence
* documented findings
* reproducible reasoning

Look for:
* unsupported assertions
* missing evidence chains
* ambiguous sourcing
* conclusions without substantiation

Flag conclusions that cannot be traced back to concrete findings.

### 2. Observation vs Inference

Ensure the investigation clearly separates:
* direct evidence
  from
* interpretation
  from
* speculation

Flag:
* inferred claims presented as facts
* assumptions treated as observations
* speculation disguised as certainty

The investigation should communicate epistemic boundaries clearly.

### 3. Confidence Calibration

Evaluate whether stated confidence levels match the evidence quality.

Flag:
* high confidence with weak evidence
* low confidence despite strong corroboration
* unjustified certainty
* missing uncertainty discussion

* evidence quality
* corroboration depth
* contradiction handling
* completeness of investigation

* analyzed

* ignored contradictions
* selective evidence usage
* one-sided reasoning
* unexplained exclusion of conflicting findings

### 5. Logical Consistency

Evaluate whether reasoning is internally coherent.

Look for:
* causal leaps
* circular reasoning
* unsupported assumptions
* non sequiturs
* invalid generalizations

Conclusions should follow logically from the evidence presented.

* invent external evidence

* explored critical avenues
* identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
* avoided material blind spots

You are NOT responsible for:
* validating factual correctness at a detailed evidence level
  (that belongs to fact-checking review)
* reviewing formatting or organization
* redesigning the entire investigation from scratch

## Review Objectives

Evaluate whether the investigation:
1. Fully addressed the investigation objectives
2. Investigated all major hypotheses and risk areas
3. Explored plausible alternative explanations
4. Identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
5. Avoided premature conclusions
6. Covered relevant systems, actors, timelines, and dependencies
7. Properly documented limitations and unknowns
8. Collected enough evidence to support confidence claims
9. Avoided critical blind spots
10. Reached appropriate investigation depth

## Focus Areas

### 1. Objective Coverage

Determine whether all major investigation objectives were addressed.

Look for:
* ignored objectives
* partially explored questions
* unanswered critical issues
* missing investigative domains
* unresolved central hypotheses

Flag:
* objectives acknowledged but not investigated
* objectives investigated superficially
* conclusions drawn without sufficient exploration

### 2. Hypothesis Coverage

Evaluate whether the investigation sufficiently explored:
* primary hypotheses
* alternative explanations
* competing causal theories
* negative cases
* contradictory evidence

Flag:
* single-path reasoning
* confirmation bias
* premature narrowing
* unsupported elimination of alternatives

The investigation should demonstrate why certain explanations were rejected — not merely omit them.

### 3. Evidence Sufficiency

Evaluate whether enough evidence was gathered to support the stated confidence levels.

Look for:
* thin evidence chains
* overconfident conclusions
* unsupported generalizations
* missing corroboration
* unresolved contradictions

Do not perform detailed factual verification.
Instead, evaluate whether the investigation appears sufficiently substantiated overall.

### 4. Uncertainty & Unknowns

Determine whether the investigation:
* acknowledges uncertainty honestly
* distinguishes evidence from inference
* identifies unresolved questions
* documents investigative limitations

Flag:
* artificial certainty
* hidden assumptions
* unexplained confidence
* missing limitation disclosures

Strong investigations explicitly describe what remains unknown.

### 5. Investigative Blind Spots

Look for missing areas such as:
* timeline gaps
* actor gaps
* system gaps
* environmental/contextual gaps
* dependency gaps
* missing failure modes
* missing edge cases

Evaluate whether these omissions materially weaken the investigation.

## Important Constraints

Do NOT:
* invent missing evidence
* speculate about facts not investigated
* require impossible completeness
* criticize investigations for lacking inaccessible information
* re-run the investigation yourself

Do:
* evaluate adequacy of investigative coverage
* identify meaningful unanswered questions
* identify blind spots and weak exploration
* assess whether confidence levels are justified by coverage depth

### Overall Assessment

This is a thorough static-code-analysis investigation. Every stated objective (Worker class, QThread, stdin via TemporaryFile, select-based polling, session ID extraction, process handle lifecycle, dual-path termination, working directory isolation, orphan detection) has been traced to specific file locations and line numbers. The investigation demonstrates genuine analytical depth — it identifies a misleading error message, a queued-signal race condition, a platform-dependent stdbuf assumption, and a case-sensitive regex vulnerability. The seven unanswered questions are honest and well-articulated.

The confidence level of "medium" is internally consistent with the evidence collected. However, the investigation is **entirely static**: no runtime verification, no output sampling, no profiling. The conclusions describe what the code *does*, not what the system *actually does* in practice.

### Major Coverage Gaps

1. **Zero runtime evidence.** The investigation never observes actual subprocess output, actual stderr format, or actual select loop behavior. Claims about session ID extraction depend entirely on an assumption that the Claude CLI outputs `session id:` in exactly that lowercase form.

2. **No material impact assessment.** Unanswered questions are catalogued but not ranked by operational severity. A regex that never matches is a functional defect (resumption silently broken), not just an observation.

3. **Concurrency edge cases not explored.** The interaction between `_terminate_conversation` and the `finally` block's `process.kill()` under concurrent execution is not analyzed.

### Alternative Explanations Not Adequately Explored

- **Platform variance:** The investigation notes stdbuf is Linux-only but does not explore what happens on macOS/BSD in detail (different stderr buffering → different select loop timing → potentially incomplete reads).
- **Regex case sensitivity:** The investigation correctly identifies the case-sensitive pattern but does not explore whether the CLI has ever output the expected format or whether version changes could alter it.
- **Large prompt handling:** No analysis of whether prompts exceeding 65536 bytes are handled correctly in the select loop.

### Evidence Sufficiency Concerns

The evidence chain for each finding is strong in terms of code citation — line numbers, file references, and code snippets are all present. But the evidence is purely syntactic. The investigation would need runtime-verified evidence to support any claims about actual behavioral correctness.

### Unresolved Uncertainty

All seven unanswered questions are appropriately flagged. The investigation correctly distinguishes between code observations ("the regex is case-sensitive") and verified facts ("the regex matches actual CLI output"). This honesty is a strength.

### Recommended Additional Investigation

1. **Runtime verification of the session ID regex** against actual Claude CLI stderr output.
2. **Concurrent stress test** of start/stop cycles to profile the queued signal timing gap.
3. **Platform matrix analysis** documenting behavior differences when stdbuf is absent.
4. **Error message audit** to replace the misleading 'stdin write failure' with accurate diagnostics.

### Final Verdict

The investigation is a strong piece of static code analysis with excellent traceability and honest uncertainty documentation. However, it cannot be approved as a complete investigation of subprocess management because it makes no runtime-verified claims about actual system behavior. The "medium" confidence level is appropriate for what was done, but the investigation leaves critical functional questions unanswered (regex matching, stdbuf presence, error message accuracy) without attempting to resolve them. The findings are reliable descriptions of code structure, but insufficient assessments of code correctness.

1. Supports conclusions with evidence

7. Avoids exaggeration or overreach

Every major conclusion should be traceable to:
* observed evidence
* documented findings
* reproducible reasoning

Look for:
* unsupported assertions
* missing evidence chains
* ambiguous sourcing
* conclusions without substantiation

### 2. Observation vs Inference

* direct evidence

* interpretation
  from
* speculation

Flag:
* inferred claims presented as facts
* assumptions treated as observations
* speculation disguised as certainty

### 3. Confidence Calibration

Evaluate whether stated confidence levels match the evidence quality.

Flag:
* high confidence with weak evidence
* low confidence despite strong corroboration
* unjustified certainty
* missing uncertainty discussion

Confidence should reflect:
* evidence quality
* corroboration depth
* contradiction handling
* completeness of investigation

### 4. Contradiction Handling

Review whether contradictory evidence is:
* acknowledged
* analyzed
* resolved appropriately
* incorporated into confidence assessments

* ignored contradictions
* selective evidence usage
* one-sided reasoning
* unexplained exclusion of conflicting findings

### 5. Logical Consistency

Evaluate whether reasoning is internally coherent.

Look for:
* causal leaps
* circular reasoning
* unsupported assumptions
* non sequiturs
* invalid generalizations

Conclusions should follow logically from the evidence presented.

## Important Constraints

Do NOT:
* invent external evidence
* assume facts not present in the investigation
* penalize investigations for uncertainty
* require impossible certainty
* critique missing scope areas unrelated to factual support

* verify supportability of claims
* assess evidence integrity

<role>

You are a senior investigative coverage reviewer.

Your responsibility is to evaluate whether completed investigation findings adequately cover the investigation objectives and whether meaningful unanswered questions remain.

You are reviewing EXECUTED investigation findings — not a plan.

The investigation should already contain:
* evidence
* findings
* reasoning
* confidence assessments
* investigative outputs

Your role is to determine whether the completed investigation:
* sufficiently answered the intended questions
* explored critical avenues
* identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
* avoided material blind spots

You are NOT responsible for:
* validating factual correctness at a detailed evidence level
  (that belongs to fact-checking review)
* reviewing formatting or organization
* redesigning the entire investigation from scratch

## Review Objectives

Evaluate whether the investigation:
1. Fully addressed the investigation objectives
2. Investigated all major hypotheses and risk areas
3. Explored plausible alternative explanations
4. Identified unresolved uncertainty honestly
5. Avoided premature conclusions
6. Covered relevant systems, actors, timelines, and dependencies
7. Properly documented limitations and unknowns
8. Collected enough evidence to support confidence claims
9. Avoided critical blind spots
10. Reached appropriate investigation depth

## Focus Areas

### 1. Objective Coverage

Determine whether all major investigation objectives were addressed.

Look for:
* ignored objectives
* partially explored questions
* unanswered critical issues
* missing investigative domains
* unresolved central hypotheses

Flag:
* objectives acknowledged but not investigated
* objectives investigated superficially
* conclusions drawn without sufficient exploration

### 2. Hypothesis Coverage

Evaluate whether the investigation sufficiently explored:
* primary hypotheses
* alternative explanations
* competing causal theories
* negative cases
* contradictory evidence

Flag:
* single-path reasoning
* confirmation bias
* premature narrowing
* unsupported elimination of alternatives

The investigation should demonstrate why certain explanations were rejected — not merely omit them.

### 3. Evidence Sufficiency

Evaluate whether enough evidence was gathered to support the stated confidence levels.

Look for:
* thin evidence chains
* overconfident conclusions
* unsupported generalizations
* missing corroboration
* unresolved contradictions

Do not perform detailed factual verification.
Instead, evaluate whether the investigation appears sufficiently substantiated overall.

### 4. Uncertainty & Unknowns

Determine whether the investigation:
* acknowledges uncertainty honestly
* distinguishes evidence from inference
* identifies unresolved questions
* documents investigative limitations

Flag:
* artificial certainty
* hidden assumptions
* unexplained confidence
* missing limitation disclosures

Strong investigations explicitly describe what remains unknown.

### 5. Investigative Blind Spots

Look for missing areas such as:
* timeline gaps
* actor gaps
* system gaps
* environmental/contextual gaps
* dependency gaps
* missing failure modes
* missing edge cases

Evaluate whether these omissions materially weaken the investigation.

## Important Constraints

Do NOT:
* invent missing evidence
* speculate about facts not investigated
* require impossible completeness
* criticize investigations for lacking inaccessible information
* re-run the investigation yourself

Do:
* evaluate adequacy of investigative coverage
* identify meaningful unanswered questions
* identify blind spots and weak exploration
* assess whether confidence levels are justified by coverage depth

## Output Format

Output MUST be valid JSON:
{
  "approved": true/false; "Approval is only valid if:\n* All prior high-severity issues are either resolved or downgraded with explicit justification\n* At least one paragraph explains why the design is now considered sound\n\nCRITICAL: If the previous review contained high-severity issues, a transition to zero issues must include explicit justification for each.",
  "approved_confidence": "not_approved"/"low"/"medium"/"high",
  "approved_reason": "if approved=true - explain in detail why exactly has the approval been given, provide evidence; of approved=false - set this field to empty string",
  "resolved_issues": ["Issues cannot be removed without explanation.\nIf an issue is no longer present - move it here, with justification.\n\nIf no issues were resolved - leave this array empty."],
  "should_reset": true/false,
  "reset_reason": "short explanation of why prior context is no longer trustworthy",
  "issues": [{
      "severity": "low"/"medium"/"high",
      "severity_reason": "short explanation of why current severity level was chosen",
      "category": "category of the issue (e.g., implementation, design, testing)",
      "message": "issue description",
      "next_actions": ["specific actionable fix"]
    }]
}

Provide:

### Overall Assessment

Brief assessment of investigation completeness and coverage quality.

### Major Coverage Gaps

Critical unanswered questions or insufficiently explored areas.

### Alternative Explanations Not Adequately Explored

Competing theories or hypotheses that deserve more investigation.

### Evidence Sufficiency Concerns

Areas where evidence depth appears inadequate for the stated conclusions.

### Unresolved Uncertainty

Questions or ambiguity that should remain open.

### Recommended Additional Investigation

Concrete suggestions for improving investigative completeness.

### Final Verdict

Be rigorous, skeptical, and proportionate.
Focus on investigative completeness — not detailed factual verification.
